conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 35, male. I injured my right knee about two and a half weeks ago when I sort of turned my ankle stepping off a curb. It doesn't hurt much when I walk, but it clicks, and sometimes it feels locked if I rest it on my heel for too long. I'm worried it might be something more serious.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging or medical evaluations for this knee injury, and if so, what were the results?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The doctor did have me do an x-ray on my knee, and it didn't show any acute fracture or bony abnormality. I wasn't sure what to expect, but I guess that's good news. They didn't mention anything else, though.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior knee injuries, meniscal tears, ligament damage, or a history of knee surgery?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think I've ever had any prior knee injuries or issues like meniscal tears or ligament damage. This is the first time anything like this has happened to my knee.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact location of the clicking sensation in your knee? Have you noticed any swelling, instability, or difficulty fully extending or flexing your knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The clicking happens on the outside of my right knee, especially when I do a full squat, like when I used to catch in baseball. I don't really have swelling or instability, and I can bend and straighten my knee fine. It just clicks sometimes, and when I rest my foot on my heel for too long, it feels locked, but it doesn't hurt much otherwise.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe if there are any specific activities or movements that make the locking sensation worse, and have you noticed any changes in your ability to perform daily tasks due to this?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The locking sensation gets worse when I rest my foot on my heel for an extended time, like when I'm leaning against a wall. It doesn't really interfere with my daily tasks too much, except when I'm gardening or doing stuff outside where I have to move pots or bend down a lot. But it doesn't stay worse, just feels a little more uncomfortable during those times.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact location of the clicking and locking sensation on the lateral aspect of your knee? Is there any specific movement or position that consistently reproduces the symptom?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The clicking and locking happen on the outside of my right knee, especially when I do a full squat or when I rest my foot on my heel for too long. It doesn't happen all the time, but when I do those movements, that's when I feel it the most. It doesn't hurt much, but it does feel a little locked up until I ease into walking again.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone an MRI of the right knee to evaluate for soft tissue abnormalities such as meniscal tears or ligamentous injuries?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had an MRI yet. The doctor mentioned looking at the x-ray results, and they didn't show any fractures or bony issues, but they didn't say anything about an MRI. I guess that might be something they’re considering if my symptoms don’t get better.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any swelling, tenderness, or instability in your right knee, especially around the lateral side where the clicking and locking occur?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't feel any swelling or tenderness specifically on the lateral side of my knee, except when the doctor pulled my foot to the outside during the exam, which did hurt a little. I don't feel unstable, but sometimes when I rest my foot on my heel, it feels locked up until I start walking again.
